title: The Breakdown: Databricks
summary: What Databricks actually does, and whether a $190 billion price tag makes sense.
cover_alt: The Breakdown: Databricks | The Private Ledger
body:
As AI improves, data becomes more valuable and one company may be uniquely situated to take advantage of this.

Databricks was founded in 2013 by a team of seven researchers with the goal of “making big data processing more accessible.” Today, it has evolved into the fifth most valuable private company in the world.

AI is central to the Databricks story and the proof is in the valuation. Less than two years ago in December of 2024 Databricks raised $10 billion in a Series J funding round that valued them at $62 billion. In August, the company closed a massive strategic funding round valuing the company at $190 billion.

Databricks is one of the most important and largest private companies and yet at the same time due to its complexity it’s one of the least understood. By way of a roadmap, this piece begins with the history of the company before explaining what exactly the company does in terms that are understandable without a degree in data science. I will then speak about the leadership, ethical questions involved and cover some of the financing before finally looking at the TAM, competition (including their rivalry with Snowflake) and valuation. We will conclude the piece by going over final thoughts and discussing a potential IPO in the future.

brief.thesis: Databricks sits at the intersection of enterprise data infrastructure and AI. The full report examines how its lakehouse model, leadership, competitive position, and valuation shape the case for the company.
takeaways: The report frames data infrastructure as a critical layer for the AI economy.
A $190 billion valuation makes both the operating opportunity and the entry price central questions.
brief.risk: A strong company can still be a difficult investment if growth, margins, or competitive advantages do not justify the valuation paid.
brief.watch: Databricks' AI monetization, revenue growth, margin trajectory, competition with Snowflake, and potential IPO timing.
